title: Subset Node Anomaly Tracking over Large Dynamic Graphs

problem.claim: The abstract treats monitoring selected nodes as a practical use case when graph structure changes over time.

gap.claim: Existing approaches focus on anomalous edges or streaming anomaly graph snapshots, while failing to quantify individual node changes over time or requiring computationally inefficient whole-graph representations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Targeted subset node anomaly tracking in evolving graphs is important for real-world applications.
Existing methods generally identify anomalous edges or anomaly graph snapshots in a streaming setting.
Edge-oriented methods cannot quantify individual node changes over time, while whole-graph representation methods are computationally inefficient.

source_observation.claim: Methods focused on anomalous edges do not quantify how individual nodes change over time.

interpretation.claim: Anomaly tracking objectives should align with the entity level at which change needs to be measured.

application.claim: For evolving graphs, consider node-level tracking when monitoring a targeted subset of entities.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not specify when edge-level detection or whole-graph representations would be preferable.

unknowns: The proposed method or system is not described.
No experiments, datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results are supplied.
The targeted node subset and evolving-graph setting are not operationally defined.
